goal: Give every docker management call (image/network inspect, network create, container stop/rm, the atexit force-remove) a default wall-clock timeout so a hung dockerd surfaces a docker timeout error within ceiling+epsilon instead of wedging the caller while it holds the lease.

relevant: packages/flywheel-container/src/flywheel_container/_docker.py -- _run_docker (line ~152) defaults timeout=None; management callers pass nothing: image_exists (~172), check_image_uid (~181), network_exists (~344), ensure_internal_network (~353), remove_container (~367), force_remove_container_sync (~376)
packages/flywheel-container/src/flywheel_container/_config.py -- exec_timeout config pattern; resolve the docker-management default ceiling consistently
packages/flywheel-container/tests/test_docker_primitives.py -- keep this suite green; mirror its docker-invocation stubbing
constraints: Apply a finite default timeout to every management call listed above under default config (no override required).
Do NOT regress already-bounded paths: start_container (timeout=120.0, line ~227) and docker exec (governed by exec_timeout) keep their existing bounds.
A hung dockerd must raise a distinguishable docker timeout error (DockerError-style), not hang.
An operator override (including unbounded/0 opt-out) must still be honored per the resolved config.
Add the pytest target so `uv run pytest -k docker_management_deadline` selects it.
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do not modify or weaken assertions in test_docker_primitives.py or test_docker_live.py.
Do not change start_container's or exec's existing timeout bounds.
Do not touch the core agent/rubric/grader or autopilot paths here.
edge_cases: Each management primitive (image_exists, check_image_uid, network_exists, ensure_internal_network, remove_container, force_remove_container_sync) raises a docker timeout error in bounded wall time when docker hangs, under DEFAULT config.
start_container and exec retain their bounds (assert unchanged) -- fixing one call site and leaving teardown callers unbounded must fail.
The atexit force_remove_container_sync path is bounded too (teardown must not wedge while holding the lease).
